exceptions.reason: The file tests that the result type follows `enabled`. The Vue composable has no `enabled` parameter: the template decides with `v-if`.

The file reads the `aria-label` of a React element that is given as `render`. In Vue the `as` prop takes a tag or a component with no props of its own, and `#render` is a slot, which is a function. A control reads its `aria-label` prop.
The cases test `resolveRenderedAriaLabel`, which reads a React element that is given as `render`.

The file reads the id of a React element that is given as `render`. It gives the id to the owner through a ref callback. A Vase UI Menu part writes its `id` prop or its default id on its element, and each part that names it names that id. A part that another part names reads the `id` of its own element from the mount on, with `useRegisteredId`.

Vase UI has no such function. The block `the parts` of this test covers the `id` of the popup and of the list that the trigger names. The case "an `id` of white space counts as no `id`" covers an `id` of white space (`VUE-93`). `packages/vue/src/menu/MenuFilter.test.ts` covers the `id` of the list that the input names. The cases that read the props of a `render` element are for React.
The file adds the matcher `toEqualDateTime`. Only the shared suite of the temporal adapters calls it, and Vase UI does not port that suite.
The helper flushes React before and after a move of the fake clock. A ported test calls `flushMicrotasks` and `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync`, which run the flushes of Vue.
The helper merges React ref objects and ref callbacks. A Vue element takes one `ref`, so a test component gives it one function that calls each setter.
`packages/vue/test/setup.ts` moves the real pointer of the browser off the page after each test that put it there. A test file thus needs no call.
`isScrollLocked` of `packages/vue/test/fixtures/scrollDocument.ts` does this work. It reads the computed overflow of the element that scrolls the page, and the marker `data-vase-ui-scroll-locked`.
